A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Horizon-Length Prediction work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the original methods, equations, figures, tables, and experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled evaluations of code completion, fixing, and reasoning, along with horizon-awareness probing and left-to-right experiments in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a multi-token prediction comparison and three design ablations in Section 5.1 and Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the normalized remaining-token target, linear head with sigmoid, L1 loss, and combined objective with weight 0.1. The two-head left-to-right adaptation already appears in v1 Appendix A.1. Newly evaluated variants are ablation controls, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training data and language coverage remain unchanged, as do SAFIM, CrossCodeEval, CrossCodeLongEval, RepoEval, Defects4J, CRUXEval, and HumanEval/MBPP including their plus versions. The new comparisons use existing SAFIM tasks.

E2.justification: v1 discusses Gloeckle et al.'s multi-token prediction only as related work. v2 evaluates a four-token prediction comparator against NTP and HLP on DeepSeek-Coder-Base 1.3B and SAFIM in Section 5.1, Table 6. Existing main-experiment comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a four-token prediction setting and controlled variations of head complexity, supervision positions, and target normalization. They explicitly reuse the Section 4 training settings and greedy SAFIM evaluation. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.2 systematically tests three central design choices: linear versus two-layer MLP heads, supervision on every token versus only the first, and normalized versus raw targets (Tables 9–11). This substantially expands design validation beyond v1's retained post-processing, probing, and left-to-right analyses.

E5.justification: v2 introduces paired t-tests at p < 0.05 for NTP versus HLP, with significance annotations across Tables 3–5, and reports a linear-versus-MLP head test in Appendix A.2. v1 has no such significance reporting. No additional training-run counts or seeds are disclosed, so additional training runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: All original numerical results are retained, including the probing and left-to-right tables renumbered to 7 and 8. New DS-1.3B SAFIM averages are 46.7 for four-token prediction, 49.7 for the MLP head, 48.5 for first-token supervision, and 34.9 for raw targets, against 47.7 for NTP and 50.0 for standard HLP. These add substantive comparator and design-sensitivity findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the formal formulation remain unchanged. The new 'Why should HLP work?' passage supplies an intuitive mechanism explanation, without adding a theorem, proof, derivation, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: HLP supports long-horizon infilling, delivers up to 24% relative improvement without dataset-specific post-processing, improves code reasoning, and adds negligible training overhead and no inference overhead.

C2.justification: v2 explains HLP through dense supervision versus the sparse end-of-insertion signal, discusses hidden-state regularization, and attributes raw-target failure to loss-scale interference. A new Defects4J footnote qualifies statistical detectability given 313 examples and roughly 30–60 solved bugs. The central planning interpretation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents implementation choices for the added experiments: predicting four future tokens, using a two-layer MLP with ReLU, restricting HLP supervision to the first token, and removing sigmoid for raw targets. Existing optimization, data-packing, and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference set and Section 6 research positioning are unchanged, including the contrast between short-horizon multi-token prediction and HLP. Section 5.1 adds empirical support for that existing position without redefining novelty or introducing a new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a localized method explanation and Appendix A.2, and reorganizes Section 5 into 'Discussion', placing the retained probing analysis under Section 5.2 after the new comparison. Most existing prose is unchanged, apart from small corrections such as removing the duplicated 'are'.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact tables, significance superscripts in Tables 3–5, and a significance explanation in Table 3's caption. The four original figures and existing table structures are retained. Tighter spacing changes placement, and the original probing and left-to-right tables become Tables 7 and 8.

improvement.justification: The new comparator and ablations provide useful evidence for HLP's design choices, while significance reporting and the Defects4J caveat improve interpretation of retained results. The gain is focused: the added comparisons cover one model on SAFIM, and paired-test sampling details remain unspecified. These additions strengthen the paper without substantially resolving its broader mechanistic claims.
